rows.title: Home Key, portal keys and waystones
rows.chapter: Wave 1 · World, order, combat and look

criteria.text: Grandpa gives the Home Key during the opening; it sits in the backpack and cannot be dropped, sold, traded or lost in a death satchel.

Using the Home Key is one tap: a ~2 s raise-and-glow animation, then arrival at the home arch; it is refused with a stated reason in combat, dialogue, cutscene, while swimming and mid-flight; free with no cooldown.

Portal keys are real inventory items; using one at its arch unlocks that portal permanently; locked arches refuse with a readable reason; retired physical crossings no longer lead between biomes (test proves portals are the only realm path).
Each live biome has 3–5 waystones activated by touch; a portal sends the player to their last activated waystone in that biome (entry point if none); activation persists through reload.

Co-op: every player has their own Home Key and it moves only that player; a portal opens for the whole session when the host world or that character has unlocked it; a guest's own unlock follows their character to another host.
Ordinary-input loop witness: deep in a biome → Home Key → use a homestead station → portal back to the waystone, with a save/reload between steps.

Traversal: nothing in Tidewake requires Fly; nothing in Cloudreach or Stormwood assumes a later legendary or relic (gate-scan test).
Per-participant legendary offers (Veridian, Abyssal Guardian, Solmane, Stormwood's legendary) still work in the new order, accept and refuse, at capacity and with space.
Earned checkpoint saves under tests/fixtures/earned_saves/ regenerated for the new boundaries; each portal sign shows its recommended level and no hidden level gate exists.

rows.title: Breakthroughs, Masters and Ascension Feasts
rows.chapter: Wave 2 · Creature power, homestead and visuals

criteria.text: Caps at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 (ceiling 60 this pass; data holds up to 100); a capped creature stops gaining levels and shows 'breakthrough needed'.

Five Masters are placed off-path and signposted: L10 mid-Meadows, L20 upper Meadows before the Warden's stronghold, L30 an outer Tidewake island, L40 a Cloudreach high perch (Fly), L50 deep Stormwood.
Each Master fight is a 1v1 with a creature of the player's choice; a win opens a chest teaching that tier's Ascension Feast once per character; a loss is retryable.
The feast needs that tier's biome materials plus one type-attuned ingredient matching the creature; it is cooked at the Kitchen and fed to one creature to lift its cap.
Each co-op participant earns their own recipe; nobody receives it twice.
A ledger proves every feast ingredient is reachable in or before its biome.

The breakthrough offers evolve or stay; staying is permanent for that tier.
Evolution preserves uid, nickname, level, bond history, IVs, traits and mastery.
The new storm bear exists via an agent-drafted reference and Meshy, larger than Staticub and taller than the trainer, with provenance recorded and an in-engine code-blind PASS; flag-gated until then.
Cannonback and Stormcapra remain wild where they already appear; Tuskroot, Ashtusk and the storm bear are not wild.

A seed teaches into trait slots unlocked at the L10, L30 and L50 breakthroughs and costs essence.
Each trait's effect applies in combat or traversal (unit test per trait); the existing bond second-trait rule is unified with this system.

rows.title: Homestead stations and upgrades
rows.chapter: Wave 2 · Creature power, homestead and visuals

criteria.text: Workbench, Forge, Kitchen, Altar, Den and Farm plots (plus chests) can be built on the homestead plot.
Forge, Kitchen, Altar and Den each take exactly one attachment per biome (4 live, 8 slots) built from biome materials; recipe tier requires the attachment.

Meadows (tier 1) attachments are available from the start; hanging a biome's relic in the Shrine Room unlocks the next tier's attachment recipes (Meadows relic → Tidewake tier, and so on; Stormwood's relic → reserved tier 5); the player then carries one chosen relic power.
Each station shows a single 'next upgrade' target; no tech tree screen is required to understand progress.
No automation: crops, smelting and cooking need the player's interaction (test).
Co-op: buildings are world-owned; tiers and recipes are personal; a guest uses the host's stations at the host's tier and keeps what they craft.
Stations read as distinct objects at the normal camera (code-blind judge).

The Forge refines Rootiron, Tidesteel, Skyglass and Stormglass plate.
One or two type-essence nodes per type sit in each biome, mostly off-route, and respawn on a configured timer.
Eight type crops grow on homestead plots; the Greenhouse (a Farm buildable, not an attachment) grows off-biome crops; every harvest is by hand.
Shed items (skyplume, sparkfur and others) drop after wins and from Den grooming; no item implies hunting or butchering (test).
The ten Tidewake water_crafting proposals are registered at runtime; four-character node contention follows MULTIPLAYER.

criteria.text: An agent-piloted normal route estimates a 15–25 hour clear; the owner's play pass confirms the range.
Essence and material ledgers: the main path reaches each band's entry without mandatory repeat grinding; optional grinding measurably speeds progress.
Four-character contention ledgers are solvent.
C2 difficulty holds for every biome band in the new order.
No exploit loop (buy/resell, rest, release farming beyond the intended rate, bounty rerolls) mints unbounded value.

rows.title: Co-op across the new loop
rows.chapter: Wave 3 · Loop, balance and release

criteria.text: A two-peer session runs hub → homestead crafting → portal → Master → feast → boss → relic hang, with each player's receipts separate.
Disconnect and rejoin at each transaction (craft, release payout, feast, key use, relic hang) neither duplicates nor loses anything.
A four-peer session completes one biome boss with every participant receiving their own key and relic.
A behind friend follows a host through an unlocked portal, and their own progress stays honest (no permanent key without the fight).
